title: Evaluation of whole-body MRI in diagnostic accuracy of extrahepatic metastases in neuroendocrine tumors compared with the gold standard SSR-PET/CT
summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the diagnostic value of MRI of the liver compared with somatostatin receptor PET/CT for staging/re-staging patients with metastatic NETs.
conditions: Neoplasm of uncertain or unknown behaviour of other and unspecified sites

interventions.name: A minimum of 20 to a maximum of 50 patients with NET eligible for study inclusion will be recruited for this study who are referred for MRI of the liver with liver-specific contrast agent and somatostatin receptor PET/CT as part of routine clinical practice. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Clinically indicated MRI examination,
Existing clinical indication for liver MRI, 
Patient's legal capacity, available written documentation of the informed consent interview and patient's consent to participate in the study,
Additional SSTR- PET-CT at the same time points (maximum 3 months time difference).
Exclusion criteria:
Impaired renal function (GFR < 30 ml/min/1.73m²),
Known intolerance of gadolinium-containing contrast agent,
Clinically or hemodynamically unstable patients,
Other contraindications to MRI examination (claustrophobia, pacemakers or other implants not compatible with 3T MRI, metal shards, etc.),
Pregnant women and nursing mothers
